en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammapaccanīyānuloma (4), Dukapaṭṭhānapāḷi (2) 20.9.
Saraṇaduka (The Pair on Taking Refuge)
Dependent on a state that is with-conflict (*saraṇa*), a state without-conflict (*araṇa*) arises by way of root-condition (*hetupaccaya*): ... one.
Dependent on a state without-conflict, a state without-conflict arises by way of root-condition: ... three.
Dependent on a state both with-conflict and without-conflict, a state without-conflict arises by way of root-condition: ... one. (Abbreviated.)

In the case of the root condition (hetu), there are five; in the object condition (ārammaṇa), two … pe … in the ripening condition (vipāka), one … pe … in the non-disappearance condition (avigata), five.
Negative (paccanīya):
Not-root (na-hetu).

Dependent on a state with conflict (*saraṇa*), a state without conflict (*araṇa*) arises by way of the not-root condition. Dependent on a state without conflict, a state with conflict arises by way of the not-root condition. (Abbreviated. Two for not-root;

three for not-object; five for not-predominance … pe … four for not-prenascence … pe … two for not-kamma … pe … one for not-nutriment, not-faculty, not-jhāna, and not-path … pe … two for not-dissociation … pe … three for not-disappearance.
(The “Conascent” section … pe … and the “Associated” section are also the same as the “Dependent” section.)
A state that is without conflict (araṇa) is a condition, by way of the root-condition (hetu-paccaya), for a state that is without conflict.

A state that is without conflict is a condition, by way of the root-condition, for a state that is without conflict. A state that is without conflict is [a condition] for a state that is with conflict...
A state that is without-conflict (anaraṇa) is a condition for a state that is with-conflict (saraṇa) and without-conflict by way of root-condition (hetu-paccaya).

A state that is not-with-conflict (na-saraṇa) is a condition for a state that is with-conflict by way of object-condition (ārammaṇa-paccaya). A state that is not-with-conflict is a condition for a state that is without-conflict by way of object-condition … [two].

A state without conflict (*na-araṇa*) is a condition for a state without conflict by way of the object-condition (*ārammaṇa-paccaya*). A state without conflict is a condition for a state with conflict by way of the object-condition ...
two. (Abbreviated. Under root: four; under object: four; under predominance:
five; under proximity: four ... pe ... under conascence: five; under mutuality: two; under dependence: seven; under decisive support: four; under prenascence and postnascence: [four].
In the case of repetition, there are two; in the case of kamma, four; in the case of result, one; in the cases of nutriment, faculty, jhāna, and path, four;
in the case of association, two; in the case of dissociation, three ... pe ... in the case of non-disappearance, seven.
A state not subject to clinging is a condition for a state subject to clinging by way of object-condition, decisive-support-condition, and prenascence-condition. (Abbreviated.)

Seven by way of not-root; seven by way of not-object ... pe ... five by way of not-coexistent, not-mutuality, and not-dependence ... pe ... six by way of not-prenascence ... pe ... five by way of not-association; four by way of not-dissociation ... pe ... four by way of not-non-disappearance.
(Just as the positive, negative, positive-negative, and negative-positive enumerations were calculated for the question-section of the Faultless Triplet, so should they be calculated here.)
